rationale: Losing a tower for nothing hands the enemy gold and opens the map in their favor.
source_excerpt: Unless you can get a tower first, or make a worthwhile trade such as the Mid lane outer for a side lane outer, you never want to give the enemy the opportunity to take a tower or destroy the armor plating.

tip: Track the enemy jungler's location while roaming.
rationale: Running into them unexpectedly can blow your cover and ruin the roam entirely.
source_excerpt: When roaming, especially if you don’t have the greatest of kill threat, you’ll need to know where the enemy Jungler is at all times.

tip: Avoid taking an aggressive route through the enemy jungle when you don't know where their jungler is.
rationale: Without that information you risk walking straight into them.
source_excerpt: Avoid going into the enemies jungle and taking an aggressive route if you don’t know where they are.

tip: Check every bush you pass while roaming for visible wards.
rationale: Missing a warded bush lets the enemy see you coming and back off in time.
source_excerpt: I recommend that you check every bush you walk past for visible signs of wards.

tip: Use a Sweeping Lens instead of face-checking bushes directly when roaming, especially on squishy champions like Lux or Zyra.
rationale: Sweeping reveals a ward or champion's silhouette without exposing you to the risk of walking in blind.
source_excerpt: If you have a Sweeping Lens available to you, you would want to use that as a substitute rather than face checking bushes directly.

tip: Path through the middle of the river while sweeping to maximize the Sweeping Lens's area of effect.
rationale: Centering your path gets the widest possible coverage from a single sweep.
source_excerpt: To maximize this technique, I would recommend that you path directly through the middle of the river so you give the Sweeping Lens the biggest area of effect.

tip: Count the visible enemy champions on the map before roaming into unclear territory — if you can account for most of them, the path is likely safer.
rationale: Accounting for four out of five enemies sharply narrows the chance of an ambush versus only seeing one or two.
source_excerpt: When in doubt, always count the numbers of enemy champions on the map. If you count most of them, say four out of five, the likelihood of your path being safe increases.

tip: Place deep wards on your way to and from lanes while roaming.
rationale: It reveals enemy positions and jungle camp availability for your whole team, not just yourself.
source_excerpt: When you’re roaming, you should try to place deep wards on your way to and from each lane.

tip: LeBlanc can deep ward safely and efficiently using her Distortion to hop walls, minimizing her time exposed in the enemy jungle.
rationale: Less time spent inside enemy territory directly reduces the risk of getting caught while warding.
source_excerpt: For example, LeBlanc can deep ward very easily thanks to her Distortion (W), which can enable her to get over walls.

tip: Immobile champions like Syndra struggle to roam and deep ward safely, since they lack dashes or leaps to escape with.
rationale: Without mobility, entering deep enemy territory to place a ward is far riskier.
source_excerpt: Syndra may find it difficult to roam and ward as she is rather immobile and has no dashes or leaps.

tip: Don't limit your warding to just your own lane — place deep wards elsewhere on the map when you're able to.
rationale: Most players only ward their own lane, leaving the rest of the map dark for their team.
source_excerpt: Many players tend to just ward their own lane and nowhere else. If you’re able to, I would highly recommend that you ward like this whenever possible.

tip: Use Scryer's Bloom and Blast Cone to adjust your roam pathing and increase your odds of getting a kill.
rationale: Both plants give you tools specifically suited to reshaping a roam mid-route.
source_excerpt: The two plants that directly help you in roaming are the Scryer’s Bloom and the Blast Cone.

tip: Use Scryer's Bloom to scout for enemy wards before roaming through an area, then reroute to avoid whatever it reveals.
rationale: Knowing which parts of the map are warded lets you choose a path that keeps you unseen.
source_excerpt: Any wards that are placed will show on the map which you can play around to ensure that you’re not spotted at any time by taking an alternative roaming route and avoiding these wards.

tip: As Support, shoot the Scryer's Bloom into the enemy jungle to make deep warding and aggressive roaming safer.
rationale: Scouting ahead of your own path reveals hidden wards before you walk into their vision.
source_excerpt: If you’re the Support, you can shoot the Scryers Bloom into the enemy’s jungle to make deep warding and aggressive roaming more successful.

tip: If you know the enemy jungler isn't on a particular side of the map, that side becomes a safer route to roam through.
rationale: Confirmed absence of the jungler removes the biggest threat to walking through their jungle.
source_excerpt: If you know that the enemy Jungler is not on one side of the map, it will be safer for you to go and walk through their jungle.

tip: Accept that roams won't always be perfectly timed — when you roam too early or too late, focus on making the best of the situation rather than tilting.
rationale: League rarely plays out exactly on paper, so adaptability matters more than chasing a perfect roam.
source_excerpt: As suggested, no matter what happens, try to make the best out of a bad situation.

tip: As a ranged support, help your ADC push the wave with auto attacks to help secure the level 2 breakpoint first.
rationale: Hitting level two before the enemy duo gives your team a large early gold and ability advantage.
source_excerpt: And if you're a ranged support, your job is going to be simple. Help your ADC push with auto attacks

tip: Look for free poke whenever the enemy walks up to contest the wave, especially against melee opponents.
rationale: Melee opponents walking up to contest are exposed to poke without being able to punish it back.
source_excerpt: look for any free poke whenever the enemy walks up, especially if your opponents are melee.

tip: Even if the enemy respects your level-2 timing, still use it to get free damage in or zone them off the wave.
rationale: A recognized power spike still forces the enemy to play cautiously, which you can convert into damage or CS denial.
source_excerpt: hitting level two first is still super important as you can use it to get some free damage or even just zone your opponents

tip: In melee-versus-melee lanes, prioritize hitting level two first, since whoever gets there first controls the lane.
rationale: The level-two power spike decides who dictates the melee-versus-melee matchup from that point on.
source_excerpt: gets there first has full control over the lane.

tip: As a melee support in a melee matchup, help your ADC push the wave to secure the level two breakpoint.
rationale: Whoever hits the breakpoint first gets full control of the lane, so contesting the push matters.
source_excerpt: So you need to be helping your ADC push.

tip: Save your support item's execute charges for the second wave, using them to instantly kill a low-health minion and set up a surprise engage.
rationale: Holding charges for the second wave lets you convert them into a burst of unexpected pressure rather than spending them early for no advantage.
source_excerpt: Save the charges for the second wave to instantly kill a minion from 50% health then look for the surprise engage.

tip: In lower elo, expect the enemy ranged support to often misplay by being too passive, and punish it.
rationale: Passive play from a ranged support at low elo opens a level-two window that would otherwise be closed.
source_excerpt: the lower Elo you are, the more likely it is that the ranged support makes the mistake of playing far too passive.

tip: Don't autopilot concede the level-two push against a ranged support — pay attention to how the enemy duo actually plays it out.
rationale: Ranged supports don't always play the contest correctly, so passive assumptions can cost you a winnable push.
source_excerpt: don't just autopilot concede the push. Actually pay attention to how the enemy duo plays it out.

tip: As a melee support who can engage from level one, like Rell, use the threat of an engage to force the level-two push in your favor.
rationale: The mere possibility of an early engage pressures the enemy duo into contesting less aggressively.
source_excerpt: especially if you're a melee champion who can engage from level one, like Rell here, use the threat of a potential engage to ensure you get the push.

tip: If you're losing the level-two push and your ADC isn't contesting it, back off, let the wave come to you, and preserve your health.
rationale: Forcing a losing push costs health for no gain when the wave will come to you anyway.
source_excerpt: So, if you are losing the push, or your ADC just doesn't care about it, that's completely fine. Just back off, let the wave come into you, and most importantly, preserve your health.

tip: Once levels equalize after conceding the early push, look for the engage — the wave will now be on your side, giving you more time to run down opponents.
rationale: A wave on your side of the map extends the chase window in your favor.
